My story

I like to work out what a device has to do before I draw it, build it quickly, and test it until I know where it fails. Most of my projects sit between anatomy, CAD, 3D printing, and the lab bench, and I’m comfortable at every step, from soldering the wires to writing the procedure so someone else can repeat the test.

I start with the people who will use a device. I’ve spent more than 60 hours observing surgeries and device use at Guthrie Hospital, and clinician feedback shapes every revision I make.

I’m looking for my next role on a medical device team where I can work across design, testing, and the processes that make a product dependable, from first requirements through verification.

All work

Nasal light-delivery device

A stent and holder cap that carry laser light deep into the nose, shaped to fit real anatomy.

Can a small stent guide laser light deep into the nasal cavity and still fit a real human nose? I started with what the clinical team needed and the limits of the anatomy, and turned both into specifications for the stent and a cap that holds the laser and probe.

I designed in SolidWorks around cadaver scans and printed every version into a nasal model to check its fit. Clinician feedback went into each revision.

The design is confidential, so these test images are blurred.

Once the fit worked, I moved to the bench. I built and calibrated a laser setup and measured optical power through porcine brain, human cadaver, and rat brain tissue, following Class 3–4 laser safety practice. Monte Carlo simulations helped predict how the photons would travel.

I documented every test and wrote the procedures so each round could be repeated and compared with the last.

The stent length and height fit the anatomy, testing showed where the tube wall needed to be stronger, and the light distributor reached its target.

Worked with: SolidWorks, 3D printing, laser safety, optical power measurement, Monte Carlo simulation, SOP writing

Anatomy you can hold

Skull and nasal cavity models built from cadaver scans.

Before a device goes near a patient, you need to see how it fits. I turned CT and MRI scans of cadaver anatomy into 3D models, separating bone from the nasal structures.

From that anatomy I designed nasal stents in SolidWorks, printed models in clear and gray resin, and tested the stents on cadaver heads to check fit. After each round I made changes.

The models now support device fit checks and preclinical cadaver evaluation.

Worked with: Materialise Mimics, 3D Slicer, SolidWorks, resin 3D printing

Heart valve delivery prototypes

More than 20 prototypes of valve and catheter-based delivery systems, designed at Cornell’s Butcher Lab.

Transcatheter aortic valve systems are small and unforgiving, and they are hard to judge from a drawing. I modeled each part in SolidWorks and printed it in SLA or FDM so the idea could be held and tested.

I used mechanical testing to tune stent geometry, materials, and tolerances, and ran failure mode analysis under ISO 14971. I also kept the design history file, tracking design inputs, outputs, and verification so every change could be traced.

More than 20 prototypes built, and a 15% improvement in stent radial strength.

Worked with: SolidWorks, SLA and FDM printing, mechanical testing, tolerancing, FMEA

Making the parts myself

Waterjet, laser cutting, and thermoforming.

I like to build what I design, because the machine teaches you things CAD doesn’t. I cut a wrench on the WAZER waterjet, laser-cut a BME ruler and hole gauge, and thermoformed a plastic part over a molded form.

Working with these processes taught me to design for how a part will actually be made.

Worked with: WAZER waterjet, Glowforge laser cutter, thermoforming, CNC mill and lathe, injection molding

Egg-grabbing robot

A gripper arm on a mecanum-wheel robot, built for a competition.

The competition scored robots on collecting eggs from straw. I designed and modeled the grabbing arm, mounted it on the robot, wired the servo motors to an Arduino, and soldered the connections so everything worked together.

The robot ran in the competition arena.

Worked with: Mechanical design, CAD, Arduino, servo motors, soldering

Algae photobioreactor

A reactor designed around surface area, light, and liquid flow.

Algae output depends on how much surface area and light the culture gets. I designed vertical columns to increase both, then set up tubing to move culture liquid between a flask and the columns, managing flow and pressure. LED lighting runs alongside.

A working reactor that circulates and lights the culture.

Worked with: Fluid handling, pressure management, prototyping

Smart coffee machine

A coffee machine paired with a smart cup that senses saliva and recommends how much caffeine to have in a day.

The idea: a cup with built-in circuits that analyze your saliva, and a machine that uses the result to tell you your daily caffeine amount. I worked on the machine side.

I designed the machine in CAD, including the internal layout, the brew area, and a removable water tank with a lid. I also managed the bill of materials so the design could move toward being built.

A complete machine model and bill of materials.

Worked with: Fusion 360, CAD assembly design, bill of materials management
